extraAngles.prompt: HOW OFFICIAL D&D DESCRIBES A PLACE — the register nearest a settlement dossier: the 2024 DMG's Greyhawk gazetteer chapter and the 2014 DMG ch. 1 (settlements, government, commerce tables), Hommlet (T1), The Keep on the Borderlands, Phandalin (Lost Mine), Vallaki (Curse of Strahd), Saltmarsh (Ghosts of Saltmarsh), the Waterdeep wards (Dragon Heist), Volo's Guide to Waterdeep (1993, the in-world guidebook register), the Mystara Gazetteers, Ptolus — reviews, close readings and designer commentary on how those texts write a town: sentence shape, what they list, what they narrate, DM-facing vs read-aloud, in-world voice vs rules voice

THE CURRENT WotC HOUSE STYLE (the sweep read the superseded 2013 v1.04a): the 'D&D Style Guide' updated January 2019 (v1.08a ©2018; freely hosted at cyborgsandmages.wordpress.com/.../dnd_house_style_guide_updated_january_2019.pdf; the DMs Guild bundle page says 'updated January 2019'), its Gender, Gender-Specific Suffixes, Gender and Fantasy Races, Headings, Sidebars, Possessives, Bulleted Lists, Appendix References, Forgotten Realms Terms ('goodsir', 'godsforsaken') and Adventuring Parties sections; the bundle's OTHER documents (the Perkins/Bilsland 'Adventure Design Guide' — the likely origin of 'here and now', 'backstory', 'credible threat'); the Adventurers League Dungeoncraft Design Guide v1.9c (2025) and the AL adventure template where boxed text is prescribed today; WotC's June 2020 statement and the Curse of Strahd / Tomb of Annihilation text revisions (Ray Winninger) as the publisher's own prose-policy acts

THE COMMUNITY USABILITY SCHOOL on adventure prose: Bryce Lynch / tenfootpole's standards page ('succinct and evocative'; 'boxed text is usually not a good thing'), Justin Alexander's 'The Art of the Key' (2014; the ogre room 'should talk about the ogre first'; 'rigid format ends up having the opposite effect') and his boxed-text pieces, Melan (Gabor Lux), Gearing, David Hartlage / DMDavid (incl. the 1979 Lost Tamoachan boxed-text dating), Trent Foster (2009) on Gygaxian prose, Gygax in his own words (the Grognardia page: 'old fashioned' boyhood reading, dictionaries and thesauruses; 'White Dwarf Interviews Gary Gygax') — what each says about read-aloud, keys, and the DM-facing sentence

SCHOLARSHIP and EDITION HISTORY of the register: Jon Peterson (Playing at the World, The Elusive Shift, Game Wizards, Fifty Years of D&D ch. 3, 'Quagmire!'), Fifty Years of D&D chapters 5 (Rowe and Howard on Holmes Basic), 15 (Cote and Saidel, race to species) and 17 (Trammell and Garcia); Antero Garcia 2017 and Aaron Trammell 2016; Fine, Mackay, Zagal and Deterding (the canonical academic texts); Shank, 'Productive Violence and Poststructural Play in the Dungeons and Dragons Narrative', Journal of Popular Culture (2015; Crossref abstract); Appelcline, Witwer, Riggs on editorial history; the Kobold Guide to Worldbuilding ('How to Design a City State, Tribe, or Nation'); Merwin's sibling columns; 4e's terse delve format vs Holmes/Moldvay/Mentzer Basic as register history
